classification.difficultyReason: Interpret each symbolic angle as a reflection or half-turn, use the supplied quadrant diagram to determine sine and cosine signs, and combine those signs for tangent. This requires routine linked use of angle symmetry and trigonometric ratios.

content.prompt: Use the diagram below to simplify the following.

spec.description: Circle centred on the intersecting Cartesian axes, with positive-axis arrowheads and x and y labels. Four open angular intervals lie outside the circle; each quadrant contains its supplied sine and cosine sign statements. The source circle is blue; its hue carries no mathematical distinction, so the editable outline uses house black. No shading.
spec.mathematics: Quadrants I–IV respectively have sine/cosine signs (+,+), (+,−), (−,−), (−,+), with intervals (0,π/2), (π/2,π), (π,3π/2), (3π/2,2π). No numeric ticks, origin label or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: All interval labels and sign statements are permanent supplied information, visible in the student edition.

answer.worked:
Reflection in the $y$-axis preserves the sine value.
$$\begin{align*}\sin(\pi-\theta)&=\sin\theta\end{align*}$$

Reflection in the $y$-axis reverses the cosine sign.
$$\begin{align*}\cos(\pi-\theta)&=-\cos\theta\end{align*}$$

Reflection in the $y$-axis preserves sine and reverses cosine.
$$\begin{align*}\tan(\pi-\theta)&=\frac{\sin\theta}{-\cos\theta}\\\tan(\pi-\theta)&=-\tan\theta\end{align*}$$

A half-turn reverses the sine sign.
$$\begin{align*}\sin(\pi+\theta)&=-\sin\theta\end{align*}$$

A half-turn reverses the cosine sign.
$$\begin{align*}\cos(\pi+\theta)&=-\cos\theta\end{align*}$$

A half-turn reverses both sine and cosine, preserving their quotient.
$$\begin{align*}\tan(\pi+\theta)&=\frac{-\sin\theta}{-\cos\theta}\\\tan(\pi+\theta)&=\tan\theta\end{align*}$$

Reflection in the $x$-axis reverses the sine sign.
$$\begin{align*}\sin(2\pi-\theta)&=-\sin\theta\end{align*}$$

Reflection in the $x$-axis preserves the cosine value.
$$\begin{align*}\cos(2\pi-\theta)&=\cos\theta\end{align*}$$

Reflection in the $x$-axis reverses sine and preserves cosine.
$$\begin{align*}\tan(2\pi-\theta)&=\frac{-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\\\tan(2\pi-\theta)&=-\tan\theta\end{align*}$$
